judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 70x70 product badge (src selo-BF-op-02_29-10-25.png) on the card for 'Vestido longo est lumiere'; its crop and the screenshot show the words 'BEST FRIDAY', and its alt is 'selo-produto' ('product seal'). claimTrue: the alt is a generic label for the kind of object and says nothing of what the image shows. elementFails: the badge is an image of text marking the item as part of the Best Friday sale; nothing else in the card says so (the card text has only '60 %', the name and prices), so 'selo-produto' does not serve the equivalent purpose. Looked for reasons it passes: the image is not the only content of the card link (the link is named by aria-label from the product name), so the link-name reading does not apply; if one treated the badge as decorative, a non-null alt like 'selo-produto' would still fail 1.1.1 (F39), so no reading makes it pass. captureDiffers: the live server HTML still carries the same flag markup (alt 'selo-produto', the same BF seal file) in its product-flag data; the card badge itself is client-rendered and the capture was rendered with styles, matching the screenshot. The claim names the real defect, so true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the e-mail field of the footer newsletter sign-up form (input id emailNews, type='mail', name='email', placeholder 'Digite seu e-mail', visual label 'E-mail' in a p element). claimTrue: it collects the user's own e-mail address and has no autocomplete attribute; the snapshot records Chromium's form issue FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for it, so the Chromium part holds too. elementFails: e-mail is one of the listed input purposes and HTML supports autocomplete, so 1.3.5 needs the purpose to be programmatically determinable; type='mail' is not a valid type (it falls back to text) and name='email' is not a means user agents rely on, so nothing identifies the purpose (H98 not met). Looked for an exception: the field asks about the user, not a third party, and no other technique is used. captureDiffers: the live server HTML has the same input, with no autocomplete. true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Switch to grid-2 layout' radio button in the gallery layout switcher, an unselected option (aria-checked=false) whose only visible content is an SVG grid icon. claimTrue: the screenshot crop shows the grid-2 and grid-3 icons as pale pink on the near-white page while the selected grid-4 icon is black; the live style sheet GridLayoutIcon.min.css sets the icon colour to #f3eaea, and to #181615 only for the --selected option, and #f3eaea on #fafafa computes to 1.13:1. elementFails: the icon is the visual information needed to identify the control, it is under 3:1, and the button is operable (not disabled, so the inactive exception does not apply); no hover or other rule raises it. Looked for reasons it could be wrong (transient state, wrong pixels, hidden control, inactive component): none holds. captureDiffers: the live HTML and CSS match the capture. true_positive.
